chapter_name: Thekas and Layakaris of Major Taals
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn to write the notation for prescribed Taals (Rupak, Jhaptal, Dhamar, etc.) and calculate their rhythmic fractions (Layakari) like Dugun, Tigun, and Chaugun.

key_vocabulary.definition: The standard set of Bols (syllables) played on the Tabla/Pakhawaj to define a Taal.
The rhythmic play or division of beats by altering the speed relative to the base tempo.
Double speed; playing two syllables in the space of one beat.
Quadruple speed; playing four syllables in the space of one beat.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A unique 7-beat Taal. Divisions: 3, 2, 2. Theka: Ti Ti Na | Dhi Na | Dhi Na. Unique feature: It is the only major Taal where the first beat (Sam) is traditionally considered Khali (indicated by a wave or '0').
A 10-beat Taal used often in Sadra and Madhya Laya Khayal. Divisions: 2, 3, 2, 3. Theka: Dhi Na | Dhi Dhi Na | Ti Na | Dhi Dhi Na. Sam is on 1, Khali is on 6.

A 14-beat Pakhawaj Taal used to accompany the Dhamar singing style. Divisions: 5, 2, 3, 4. Theka: Ka Dhi T | Dhi T | Dha - | Ga Ti T. It has a slightly asymmetrical, bouncing gait suited for describing Lord Krishna's Holi.

To write Dugun (double speed), combine two Bols under one crescent curve (e.g., `Dha_Ge`). To write Tigun (triple speed), group three Bols per beat. For Chaugun (quadruple speed), group four Bols per beat. The remaining layout of Vibhags, Sam, and Khali remains exactly the same.

fun_activity.title: 🧮 The Dugun Math Trick
fun_activity.instructions: To write the Dugun of a 10-beat Taal (Jhaptal), you need to fit the whole Theka in the last 5 beats (since it's double speed). So, write the normal Theka for beats 1 to 5, and then write the Dugun (two bols per beat) from beat 6 to 10!

exam_tips: 📌 Rupak Taal's 'Sam' being a 'Khali' is a favorite trick question. Always mark beat 1 with '0' (or 'X' as an exception based on your specific school's teaching, but Khali is standard).
📌 When writing Layakari, DO NOT change the position of the Vibhag lines (|) or the Tali/Khali signs. Only the number of Bols inside the beats changes.
📌 Dhamar has 14 beats with 4 Vibhags (5-2-3-4). Do not confuse it with Deepchandi (which is 14 beats but 3-4-3-4).
quick_recap: ⭐ Dugun means 2 notes/syllables per beat; Tigun means 3; Chaugun means 4.
⭐ Jhaptal has a symmetrical structure (2-3-2-3) making it very popular for medium-paced compositions.
⭐ Always draw the crescent moon shape beneath the syllables to indicate they are grouped in a single beat during Layakari.
